visual_action: The video displays a static screenshot of a tweet from an account named 'FactPost'. The tweet includes a split image of Donald Trump and a hand pumping gasoline. After a few seconds, the video cuts to a close-up, color-saturated photo of Donald Trump, which remains on screen for the rest of the clip.

cast.name: Donald Trump
cast.evidence: He is pictured in the tweet screenshot and in a follow-up close-up photo. The on-screen text of the tweet also names him directly: 'This comes after Trump launched strikes on Iran...'

cast.name: FactPost
cast.evidence: The name 'FactPost' and handle '@factpostnews' are displayed as the author of the tweet shown in the video.

cast.name: Iran
cast.evidence: The tweet text mentions 'Trump launched strikes on Iran'.

on_screen_text.text: Average U.S. gas prices have jumped $0.11 overnight, rising to $3.11 a gallon.
This comes after Trump launched strikes on Iran, causing sharp rises in crude futures.

spoken_summary: There is no spoken dialogue. The audio consists of music with a chanted vocal hook.
audio_music: The video is set to the high-energy reggaeton track 'Gasolina' by Daddy Yankee, which plays throughout. The song's title, which means 'Gasoline', thematically connects to the video's subject of gas prices, creating a mocking and energetic tone.
editing_pacing: The editing is a simple slideshow, consisting of one static screenshot followed by a quick cut to a second static photo.
manipulation_or_satire: The video presents a fabricated tweet from a non-existent or non-credible news source called 'FactPost' to create a false claim about Donald Trump's impact on gas prices. Additionally, the final photo of Trump appears to be color-saturated to exaggerate his skin tone as a form of visual mockery.
central_claim: Donald Trump is responsible for a recent spike in U.S. gas prices due to his actions against Iran.
intended_effect: To generate anger towards Donald Trump by blaming him for rising gas prices, and to mock him.
